text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: ALERT fired: inference-queue.backlog_high (P2) for service `inference-queue` — queue depth > 1200 for >2m. Links: https://pd.redwood.example/incidents/INC12345 :rotating_light:

Maya P.: ack'd on PagerDuty, jumping in. seeing 5xx downstream retries increasing.

Sanjay K.: on it. first glance — autoscaler not launching new pods. HPA target CPU at 80% but node pools exhausted.

Jordan L.: can you paste `kubectl get hpa -n inference` and nodepool status?

Sanjay K.: pasted logs:```
NAME                 REFERENCE             TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-processor  Deployment/inference   120%/80%    4         40        12
```
Node pool status: `gke-inference-pool` at 100% capacity, 0 pending nodes, autoscaler unable to allocate new due to quota.

Leo C.: Customer impact? any errors surfaced to customers?

Maya P.: Observability: increase in 429s and request queue latency for hosted API customers. Spike in token latency for long gen jobs. Some customers seeing timeouts at 30s. Pagerduty notes: 2 major customers reporting degraded perf.

Maria R.: ETA for quota bump from cloud? We don't have one yet — we have reserved capacity but we hit ephemeral spike from a churn of long requests.

Sanjay K.: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporary rate-limit long-running requests via edge policy; 2) route low-priority tenants to degraded region (eu-west fallback); 3) reduce max_batch_size and prefer shorter sequences to free GPU slots; 4) manual scale up of dedicated emergency pool (requires infra runbook).

Maya P.: do the rate-limit change first — quick config patch. I can roll it. Jordan, can you prepare the edge rule?

Jordan L.: prepping rule now. Proposed snippet:```
# edge policy
match: request.path == "/v1/generate" && request.headers["x-seq-len"] > 512
action: rate_limit: 2r/s
```
Applying to /v1/generate on hosted-prod-low-priority.

Sanjay K.: while Jordan pushes that, I'm opening a manual scale request to infra: `infra@` with subject "URGENT: temporary quota bump / emergency nodes for inference". Posting runbook commands below:```
# manual node add (requires infra perms)
gcloud container clusters resize redwood-inference --node-pool gke-inference-pool --num-nodes 60 --zone us-central1-a
```
Note: needs approval, will take ~6-8m to provision.

Maya P.: Jordan — after patch, please post response codes/counts. We'll monitor queue depth.

(2m later) Jordan L.: edge policy deployed :white_check_mark:. Early telemetry: 30% drop in incoming long-seq requests. Queue growth slowed but still at ~900.

Leo C.: any quick internal routing we can do to offload to Dedicated pool for high-SLA tenants?

Sanjay K.: yes, we can temporarily divert requests for customers with header `x-cust-tier: premium` to dedicated-inference-svc. Doing manual routing rule change now.```
PATCH /routing/service
{
  "match": "request.headers['x-cust-tier']=='premium'",
  "route": "dedicated-inference-svc"
}
```
Applying — will be effective in ~15s.

Maya P.: good. Maria, please notify CS about the routing change and that premium customers should see improvement. Include guidance to retry.

Maria R.: CS notified via channel and pinged the two reporting customers. Keeping message: "We routed premium traffic to dedicated pool to mitigate latency. We're monitoring; ETA for full recovery variable."

(4m later) incident-bot: :information_source: Autoscaler event: scale-up attempted but failed due to quota: "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Insufficient CPU quota". Attempted 8 extra nodes.

Sanjay K.: Infra responded: quota increase pending approval, but they can spin emergency nodes from warm pool (if we approve cost override). What's the cost threshold?

Maya P.: approve emergency warm-pool usage. Cost > normal but reduces customer impact. Maria, confirm with leadership?

Maria R.: leadership notified via slack DM and approved emergency warm-pool use for up to 4 hours. Posting approval ID: LD-2026-77.

Sanjay K.: initiating warm pool attach:```
# attach warm pool nodes
infra-cli attach-warm-pool --cluster redwood-inference --pool warm-inference-1 --count 12
```
(1m later) S: warm pool attach succeeded, nodes available. HPA now scales replicas to 28. Queue depth down to 320.

Jordan L.: still seeing some 500s but majority are now 200/202. Token latency median improving.

Leo C.: Customer impact summary so far for incident ticket: "Partial degradation for hosted API customers between 18:22 and present. Increased 429/30s timeouts affecting long sequence requests; mitigations deployed: edge rate-limiting for >512 tokens, routing premium tenants to dedicated pool, warm-pool nodes attached. Current queue stabilizing."

Maya P.: agreed. Let's keep incident state: triage -> mitigation -> monitoring. If queue <200 and errors <1% for 5m, we'll de-escalate.

(10m later) incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert resolved: inference-queue.backlog_high cleared. Final queue depth: 78.

Maya P.: handing off to SRE rotation for post-incident follow-up. @Sanjay K., @Jordan L. add to postmortem: root cause likely burst of long-sequence generation requests combined with node pool quota exhaustion and HPA max limits. Action items: 1) increase nodepool quota / warm pool baseline; 2) autoscaler tuning — allow opportunistic pre-provisioning; 3) make rate-limit rule as safety net; 4) automated diversion for premium tiers when queue>threshold; 5) validate alert thresholds to reduce noise.

Sanjay K.: taking on postmortem. Will open INC12345 in GH and assign.

Jordan L.: marking runbook steps we executed in incident doc. Will link to logs and dashboards.

Maria R.: CS will send customer update template.

Maya P.: thanks everyone. Closing Slack thread once postmortem is created. :thumbsup:
